INDICATION: ___ female with right lower quadrant 
tenderness, history of pancreatitis and Cesarean section in 
___. 
  
COMPARISON: ___. 
  
TECHNIQUE: Helical MDCT images were acquired from the lung bases 
through the greater trochanters with intravenous and oral 
contrast. 5 mm coronal, 
sagittal, and axial multiplanar reformats were generated. 
  
FINDINGS: Mild atelectasis is noted at the lung bases. There are 
no pleural effusions. The heart is normal in size, without 
pericardial effusion. Note is made of a small sliding hiatal 
hernia. 
  
ABDOMEN: The liver enhances homogeneously, without focal lesions 
identified on this single phase examination. The gallbladder is 
partially collapsed.  The pancreas is normal. There is no intra- 
or extra-hepatic biliary ductal dilatation. The spleen is normal 
in size. 
The adrenals are normal. The kidneys enhance and excrete 
contrast promptly 
and symmetrically, without masses or hydronephrosis. 
PELVIS: The bladder is distended with urine and appears normal. 
The uterus 
has a lobulated appearance with avid contrast enhancement, 
suggestive of 
underlying fibroids. Prominent venous collaterals are present, 
which may 
relate to pelvic congestion syndrome; please correlate 
clinically. 
GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is filled with contrast and 
ingested contents.  There is a partial small-bowel obstruction, 
with dilation of duodenal and jejunal loops to 2.5-3 cm. A 
relative transition point is present in the left lower quadrant 
(2:38 and 300B:24). Of note, there is acute angulation of bowel 
at this level, suggesting tethering by postoperative adhesions. 
Oral contrast does not pass this point. There is relative 
decompression of distal jejunal and ileal loops. 
The appendix is nondilated at 6 mm, without wall thickening or 
fat stranding to suggest acute inflammation. The colon and 
rectum are filled with fluid and retained fecal material, 
excluding high-grade bowel obstruction. Two nonspecific coarse 
calcifications are noted in the region of the cecum. There is no 
free intraperitoneal air or fluid. 
 Retroperitoneal and mesenteric lymph nodes are not 
pathologically enlarged. BONES: No suspicious lytic or sclerotic 
osseous lesions are identified. 
  
IMPRESSION: 
1. Partial small-bowel obstruction with relative transition 
point in left 
abdomen, likely secondary to postoperative adhesions. This was 
reported to Dr. ___ on ___ at 10:45 am. 
2. Probable fibroid uterus, with prominent venous collaterals 
that could 
represent pelvic congestion syndrome in the correct clinical 
setting. 

 
Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo F with chronic pancreatitis presenting with a partial SBO 
due to adhesions.
.
The patient presented wtih abdominal pain. She was found on 
abdominal x-ray and CT to have a partial SBO probably due to 
prior adhesions. In addition, she has chronic pancreatitis 
thought due to sphincter of Oddi dysfunction. Admission labs 
were within normal limits. She was seen by the surgery consult 
team. With conservative management of bowel rest, IV fluids, 
anti-emetics and pain control, the patient had good clinical 
improvement with reduced pain, successful passage of gas and 
multiple bowel movements and ability to tolerate PO's. By the 
day of discharge she was tolerating a full diet without pain and 
taking PO meds. The patient will follow-up with her PCP and 
gastroenterology.
.
The remainder of the ___ medical issues, including 
depression and GERD were managed with continuation of her home 
med regimen.
.
The patient also had headache complaints and self-reported 
associated nausea and vomiting with this. She denied having a 
history of headaches though is on home medications used to treat 
migraines. This will be further followed-up as an outpatient.
